steps: Write down the oven settings: 350F, 25 minutes.
Lower the temperature: 350 minus 25 is 325F, and the time stays 25 minutes.
Or shorten the time: 25 × 0.75 = 18.75, rounded to 19 minutes, at the same 350F.

formula.text: Pick one, never both. Lower the temperature: air fryer temp = oven temp minus 25F, and the time stays the same. Or shorten the time: keep the oven temperature and check at oven time × 0.75. For baked goods at 350F for 25 minutes: either 325F for 25 minutes, or 350F and check at about 19 minutes.

title: Oven to Air Fryer: Cakes and Bakes
tutorial: Small bakes are the quiet talent of the air fryer. Muffins, cookies, and a small banana bread bake well in a pan that fits the basket, and they bake faster than the oven does. A bake that goes in at 350F for 25 minutes air fries two ways: 325F for the full 25 minutes, or 350F and check at about 19 minutes.

The top is the thing to watch. The heating element sits just above the food, so the top of a cake browns much faster than the centre sets. If the top darkens early, tent the pan loosely with foil and let the centre finish. The foil goes on with the food holding it down, never loose in an empty basket, because the fan lifts loose foil into the element.

Bakes are also the food where the rule bends most. Some baking guides drop the temperature by 50F instead of 25F, because batter rises and sets differently in moving hot air. The lower-temperature option uses the standard 25F drop. If your bakes keep browning too fast on top, drop another 25F next time and keep the full oven time.

Use a pan that fits with air around it. The basket needs space for the hot air to move, so a pan that touches the sides bakes unevenly. A six-inch round pan fits most baskets, and silicone muffin cups fit where a metal tin does not. Fill the pan no more than two thirds full, because batter rises toward the element.

The toothpick test still decides. A cake is done when a toothpick in the centre comes out with a few moist crumbs, not wet batter. The converted time gets you close. The toothpick tells you when to stop.
